findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: web-search, web-contents, web-scrape, web-map, cors-check, og-preview, curl-to-code · Private data: dns-lookup, mail-auth, security-txt, enrich-url, wrangler-lint, mcp-config-validate, claude-md-lint, slash-command-scaffold, token-count, chunk-text, dataset-validate, prompt-lint, url-parse, cors-check, openapi-lint · Public sink: pii-redact, claude-md-lint, webhook-verify · Destructive: wrangler-lint, dataset-validate.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: web-search, web-contents, web-scrape, web-map, cors-check, og-preview, curl-to-code · Private data: dns-lookup, mail-auth, security-txt, enrich-url, wrangler-lint, mcp-config-validate, claude-md-lint, slash-command-scaffold, token-count, chunk-text, dataset-validate, prompt-lint, url-parse, cors-check, openapi-lint · Public sink: pii-redact, claude-md-lint, webhook-verify · Destructive: wrangler-lint, dataset-validate

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
